headline: RESOLUTION OF OPEN QUESTION (0600-03 sub-item h) -- UKMTO Warnings 199-26/200-26 are two separate Nov 7 Hormuz incidents
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the resolution] Two time-late UKMTO warnings published Nov 8 disclose SEPARATE tanker incidents on the evening of Nov 7, both distinct from the Nov 5 Velos Sapphire explosion (0500-01): (1) Warning 199-26: tanker on fire ~8nm NW of Khasab, Oman, 19:20 UTC Nov 7, crew evacuated;…
sources: UKMTO Warnings 199-26 and 200-26; Seatrade Maritime; DeepDraft SITREP Nov 9
fault_line: Mines or missiles -- and who is actually stopping ships in Hormuz: Iran's declared blockade, or a shadow war nobody claims?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the resolution] Two time-late UKMTO warnings published Nov 8 disclose SEPARATE tanker incidents on the evening of Nov 7, both distinct from the Nov 5 Velos Sapphire explosion (0500-01): (1) Warning 199-26: tanker on fire ~8nm NW of Khasab, Oman, 19:20 UTC Nov 7, crew evacuated; (2) Warning 200-26: a second outbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, 20:20 UTC Nov 7, crew safe, identity/flag/cargo/damage undisclosed. Seatrade Maritime: this brings to NINE the number of vessels confirmed attacked by Iran in the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf since the start of November; JMIC retains a SEVERE threat assessment. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM] IRGC Navy says THREE oil tankers caught fire Sunday after hitting mines on an 'unauthorized' route (two named in its first statement, a third added later via Fars); Reuters/AFP could not independently verify, and AFP notes it cannot confirm whether the various reports reference the same incidents. [UNRESOLVED IDENTITY CONFLICT] Online reports tentatively identify the Khasab-fire vessel as NAVIG8 MESSI (IMO 9482859) per DeepDraft; Manoto's Nov 6 carousel names 'Louiz 1' as hit by two attached mines near Musandam on Nov 7. Neither identification is confirmed by UKMTO -- do not state either as fact.
sections.what_verified: UKMTO warnings (T1) for the two incidents; AFP wire (T1) for the IRGC three-fire claim and the explicit non-confirmation; Seatrade Maritime and DeepDraft (undeclared tiers -- attribution only, do not count toward corroboration).
sections.what_disputed: AFP: unable to confirm whether the IRGC's three-fire reports, the UKMTO Khasab fire, the UKMTO projectile strike and the UAE's rescue of 22 people from a burning vessel in the Gulf of Oman reference the same incidents. Reuters could not independently verify the IRGC mine claims. The UAE rescue of 22 remains unlinked to any named vessel. Trump told CBS the Strait of Hormuz is 'open' with 'ships going through' -- against a counted 7-day Hormuz average of 4.43 transits/day (PortWatch, STALE, obs. Nov 1) vs a 2025 baseline of 85.53/day.
sections.why_matters: Nine ships hit since November 1 -- and the two latest attacks are not the one you heard about. The warnings name the time and the place; the ships' names are still a fight.
sections.context: Background: RESOLUTION OF OPEN QUESTION (0600-03 sub-item h) -- UKMTO Warnings 199-26/200-26 are two separate Nov 7 Hormuz incidents, distinct from Velos Sapphire; Seatrade counts 9 vessels attacked since Nov 1; IRGC tally now 3 fires, third unverified; vessel identities conflict (NAVIG8 MESSI vs Louiz 1)
